project:
-- Released Keiro 0.19, Kiroku 0.9 (kiroku-store-migrations 0.6), Kioku 0.8,
-- Shibuya 0.10, pg-migrate 1.2 and PGMQ 0.6.1.1. Both Cabal and the shared Nix
-- channel must select this cohort; see docs/adr/018. Kiroku 0.9 requires
-- migration 0012 before any 0.9 process appends, and 0.8 writers fail after it:
-- the global database needs a stop-writers cutover, never a rolling deploy.
index-state: 2026-09-26T18:09:31Z
packages:
  rei-core
  rei-cli
  rei-api-contract
  rei-api-client
  rei-api

-- The generated keiro-dsl conformance runner. keiro-dsl writes the package
-- beside the generated layer on every `just keiro-scaffold`; the glob keeps
-- cabal.project from having to name a path the generator owns.
optional-packages:
  rei-core/src/keiro-dsl-conformance.workspace.*/*.cabal

with-compiler: ghc-9.12.4
test-show-details: direct
tests: True

package hasql-dynamic-statements
  tests: False

-- RTS tuning for faster GHC compilation
-- -A128m: larger allocation area reduces GC frequency
-- -qg: disable parallel GC (single-threaded GC is faster for compilation workloads)
-- -n4m: larger nursery chunk size
program-options
  ghc-options:
    +RTS
    -A128m
    -qg
    -n4m
    -RTS

-- Parallel module compilation
jobs: $ncpus
-- Force crypton >= 1.1 (which uses ram, not memory). pg-migrate-import-hasql-
-- migration declares `crypton >=1.1 && <1.2` for the legacy MD5 checksums it
-- verifies when importing a predecessor ledger. http-client-tls < 0.4 caps
-- crypton below 1.1 via `crypton < 1.1`, so lift that too. The dhall
-- `use-http-client-tls` flag pins http-client-tls < 0.4, so disable it.
--
-- The three `shikumi* == ...` equalities were removed by ExecPlan 224. They existed
-- because a source-repository-package block supplies whatever version its tag holds, so
-- the equality asserted the tag was the one the comment claimed. With both families now
-- resolved from Hackage that assertion has no subject. Rei names no shikumi package in
-- any .cabal file -- it imports no Shikumi module -- so the versions are selected by
-- kioku-core 0.6.0.0's `shikumi ^>=0.4.0.0` and `shikumi-trace ^>=0.3.0.0`, by
-- shikumi-trace 0.3.0.0's `shikumi-cache ^>=0.2.0.0`, and by the frozen index-state.
-- See docs/adr/018, rule 2: a constraint without its own reason documents nothing.
constraints:
  crypton >= 1.1,
  http-client-tls >= 0.4,
  dhall -use-http-client-tls,
  blake3 -avx512 -avx2 -sse41 -sse2

package blake3
  ghc-options: -optc-DBLAKE3_USE_NEON=0

-- Package-qualified allow-newer. ADR 016 requires each entry to name the bound it
-- lifts and what declared it, why the breakage does not reach Rei, the evidence
-- that was run, and the release that retires it. ExecPlan 228 brought the block to
-- that standard and deleted the six entries whose removal no longer changed the
-- solved plan: proto-lens:base, proto-lens:ghc-prim, proto-lens:deepseq,
-- proto-lens-runtime:base, http-conduit:http-client-tls, and haxl:time (haxl is not
-- in the install plan at all). Evidence for the deletions: `cabal build all
-- --dry-run` solves with all six absent.
--
-- The formatter hoists comments out of a field's value list, so the six
-- justifications below cannot sit beside their entries. They appear in the SAME
-- ORDER as the list that follows them; keep it that way when adding or removing one.
allow-newer:
  -- fuzzyfind:containers -- lifts the `containers == 0.6.*` upper bound declared by
  -- fuzzyfind 3.0.2. GHC 9.12.4 ships containers 0.7 as a boot library, so the bound
  -- cannot be satisfied by downgrading. fuzzyfind imports only Data.Sequence, whose
  -- API is unchanged across 0.6-to-0.7; that release's breaking changes are in the
  -- Data.Map / Data.IntMap surface fuzzyfind never touches. Evidence: rei-cli builds
  -- and `cabal test all` passes with fuzzyfind linked, and removing the entry makes
  -- the solver reject the plan. Remove when fuzzyfind publishes bounds admitting
  -- containers 0.7.
  -- link-canonical:http-client-tls -- lifts the `http-client-tls >=0.3 && <0.4`
  -- upper bound declared by link-canonical 0.1.0.0. Rei forces http-client-tls >= 0.4
  -- in the constraints block above, because crypton 1.1 (needed by
  -- pg-migrate-import-hasql-migration for legacy MD5 ledger checksums) is only
  -- admitted by http-client-tls 0.4. The 0.3-to-0.4 change is a TLS-manager
  -- construction change; link-canonical calls only `TLS.newTlsManager`, the default
  -- manager, whose signature is unchanged. Evidence: `cabal test all` passes with the
  -- link canonicalisation suite linked. Remove when link-canonical publishes bounds
  -- admitting http-client-tls 0.4.
  -- link-canonical:generic-lens -- lifts the `generic-lens >=2.2 && <2.3` upper bound
  -- declared by link-canonical 0.1.0.0; the plan resolves generic-lens 2.3.0.0.
  -- link-canonical uses only Data.Generics.Labels, the orphan `#field` instances,
  -- which 2.3 leaves unchanged. Evidence: as above -- and removing the entry makes
  -- the solver report `link-canonical => generic-lens>=2.2 && <2.3`. Remove when
  -- link-canonical publishes bounds admitting generic-lens 2.3.
  -- kiroku-cli:http-client-tls -- lifts the same `http-client-tls >=0.3 && <0.4`
  -- bound, declared twice by kiroku-cli 0.2.0.6 (library and executable stanzas),
  -- against the same forced http-client-tls >= 0.4. kiroku-cli imports only
  -- `tlsManagerSettings` and passes it to `newManager`; both are unchanged in 0.4.
  -- Evidence: `just build` and `just test` pass with kiroku-cli in the plan. Remove
  -- when kiroku-cli publishes bounds admitting http-client-tls 0.4.
  -- claude:http-client-tls -- lifts the `http-client-tls >=0.3 && <0.4` upper bound
  -- declared by `claude` 1.5.0, the Anthropic SDK that baikai-claude builds on.
  -- Rei forces http-client-tls >= 0.4 in the constraints block above, because
  -- crypton 1.1 (needed by pg-migrate-import-hasql-migration for legacy MD5 ledger
  -- checksums) is only admitted by http-client-tls 0.4. The 0.3-to-0.4 change is a
  -- TLS-manager construction change that `claude` does not depend on: it uses the
  -- default manager settings only. Evidence: the full rei-core and rei-cli suites,
  -- including the three Baikai backend specs, run on the resolved plan by ExecPlan 223
  -- and re-run by ExecPlan 224. Remove when `claude` publishes bounds admitting
  -- http-client-tls 0.4.
  -- baikai-kit:crypton -- lifts the `crypton ^>=1.0` upper bound declared by
  -- baikai-kit 0.3.0.0 (revision 0; no metadata revision has widened it). Rei forces
  -- crypton >= 1.1 in the constraints block above. crypton 1.1's breaking change is the
  -- switch from `memory` to `ram` for secure byte arrays; baikai-kit uses only the
  -- hashing surface (Crypto.Hash) whose API is unchanged across that boundary.
  -- Evidence: rei-cli builds and its suite passes with baikai-kit linked, and
  -- `rei kit` -- the only consumer -- is exercised by ExecPlan 223's acceptance and by
  -- ExecPlan 224's rerun. Remove when baikai-kit publishes bounds admitting crypton 1.1.
  --
  -- Baikai 0.7 admits http-client-tls 0.4 and baikai-claude 0.7 admits crypton 1.1
  -- (>=1.0 && <1.2), so their former exceptions stay retired.
  fuzzyfind:containers,
  link-canonical:http-client-tls,
  link-canonical:generic-lens,
  kiroku-cli:http-client-tls,
  claude:http-client-tls,
  baikai-kit:crypton

-- ============================================================================
-- Released Keiro/Kiroku/Kioku/Shibuya/PGMQ/pg-migrate/keiki cohort now resolves
-- entirely from Hackage (MasterPlan 19, EP-1). The former git source-repository
-- pins for keiro, keiro-core, keiro-migrations, keiro-pgmq, kiroku-store,
-- kiroku-store-migrations, kiroku-cli, kiroku-metrics, kiroku-otel,
-- shibuya-kiroku-adapter, shibuya-core, shibuya-pgmq-adapter, pg-migrate (and its
-- embed/cli/import-codd/import-hasql-migration/test-support siblings), keiki,
-- keiki-codec-json, and the ../../kioku local packages (kioku-api, kioku-core,
-- kioku-migrations) are all removed. The bounds in rei-core.cabal and
-- rei-cli.cabal select the released versions.
-- ============================================================================
-- The tan-commons source pin was removed by MasterPlan 27 EP-5. Its four subdirs
-- left one at a time: tan-commons-migration with MasterPlan 19 EP-7, then
-- tan-commons-config and tan-hasql with EP-3 (Rei owns that code as
-- Rei.Config.Pg), and finally tan-aeson and tan-commons-time, which no .cabal
-- file named and no module imported. scripts/dependency-closure-audit.sh fails
-- if any of them comes back.
--
-- typeid-hs (topagentnetwork fork; not on Hackage). Since the four-package split
-- the repository root has no .cabal file, so both Cabal and Nix must name the
-- subdirectories. typeid-hs-pg-migrate is the native pg-migrate component
-- (ExecPlan 227); typeid-hs-sql supplies the SQL bytes the history import
-- reconciles against. The deprecated typeid-hs-hasql-migration backend was dropped
-- by the same plan's Milestone 4, and with it the hasql-migration source pin.
source-repository-package
  type: git
  location: https://github.com/topagentnetwork/typeid-hs
  tag: 7164a74c490cc92ffe73a315d827c9515de125d3
  subdir:
    typeid-hs-sql
    typeid-hs-pg-migrate

source-repository-package

-- The codd and codd-extras source pins were removed by MasterPlan 19 EP-7.
-- Nothing in the closure needs them any more:
--
--   * No Rei module imports `Codd`, and predecessor Codd history is *imported*,
--     never replayed. The adapter that does the importing, pg-migrate-import-codd,
--     reads the old ledger with Hasql and does not depend on codd.
--   * keiro-migrations 0.3 puts every codd / codd-extras dependency behind its
--     `legacy-codd-tools` flag, which defaults to False -- "the normal pg-migrate
--     closure excludes these dependencies". kiroku-store-migrations 0.3 and
--     kioku-migrations 0.1 do not name them at all.
--
-- Do not reintroduce them without also updating scripts/legacy-migration-audit.sh,
-- which fails if an execution path comes back.
-- The hasql-migration source pin was removed by MasterPlan 27 EP-4. Its only
-- consumer in the closure was typeid-hs's deprecated hasql backend, and TypeID now
-- installs through typeid-hs-pg-migrate as an ordinary component of the composed
-- plan. Nothing depends on the fork any more.
--
-- pg-migrate-import-hasql-migration is a DIFFERENT package and stays: it is the
-- Hackage decoder that reads a legacy hasql-migration ledger, which is how both
-- persistent databases explain their imported history -- including the four TypeID
-- rows EP-4 adopted. See docs/adr/011 and docs/adr/024.
--
-- The hasql-notifications source pin was removed by MasterPlan 27 EP-5. No .cabal
-- file named it and no module imported Hasql.Notifications; it had no Nix overlay
-- entry and no flake input either, so the Nix build had never needed it.
